parole.testo: Possibly from Latin de ex pressum, or more likely from Old Catalan despuix, despuis, depuis (itself from Latin de post) + aprés.
Borrowed from Latin stramonium, the species name, from Old Catalan estremonia, alteration of astronomia.

parole.significato: one, people, someone (an unspecified individual: indefinite personal pronoun)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Catalan hom, from the nominative case of Latin homō (“man”). Its pronominal use is of Germanic origin. Compare Old English man (“one, they, people”), reduced form of Old English mann (“man, person”); French on; German man (“one, they, people”); Dutch men (“one, they, people”). Dou

Ultimately from Latin sine, possibly conflated with absentia, or more likely from sens, itself from Old Catalan sen (with an adverbial -s-), from Latin sine. Compare French sans, Occitan sens, Italian senza.
